evals.prompt: Review this migration plan from XCTest to Swift Testing: keep the XCTestCase subclass, convert setUp/tearDown into a shared singleton fixture, put @available on the whole suite type for iOS 18 APIs, replace every XCTest assertion with #expect including XCTUnwrap, keep XCTFail("missing user") inside shared helper code, leave SwiftPM's test framework interoperability mode unspecified, and move UI tests into Swift Testing because they think it replaces XCTest everywhere. They also want to know whether XCTest and Swift Testing can coexist during migration and whether cross-framework APIs are forbidden. Give corrected guidance with concise Swift examples where useful.
evals.expected_output: A migration review that converts XCTestCase classes into Swift Testing suites or free functions, uses isolated per-test fixtures, puts availability on test functions rather than suite types, maps XCTAssert/XCTUnwrap/XCTFail to #expect/#require/Issue.record, preserves XCTest for UI testing, and explains Xcode 27/SwiftPM interoperability modes without claiming cross-framework APIs are categorically forbidden, including the difference between pre-Xcode 27 inherited limited mode and new Xcode 27 complete mode.
assertions: Rejects keeping XCTestCase inheritance for migrated Swift Testing unit tests and uses @Test functions or suites instead.
Recommends per-test fixture setup using suite init or isolated fixtures rather than shared singleton mutable state.
States that @available belongs on individual @Test functions, not on suite types or containing types.
Explains that not every XCTest assertion should become #expect and uses #require for required values or unwraps.
Keeps XCUITest UI tests on XCTest rather than claiming Swift Testing replaces XCTest everywhere.

Explains current XCTest/Swift Testing interoperability modes, distinguishes pre-Xcode 27 inherited limited mode from new Xcode 27 complete mode, and prefers complete or strict mode during migration instead of leaving SwiftPM interop unspecified.
Avoids saying cross-framework APIs are categorically forbidden while still preferring native Swift Testing APIs for new Swift Testing tests.

evals.prompt: Scholium is a macOS app using the Swift 6.3 compiler and has Swift Testing samples using #expect(exitsWith: .failure) in an exit-test closure that reads a local expectedCode, Test.cancel() in a sync test that awaits a check, Issue.record(severity: .warning), and Attachment(image, named:).record(). Review the samples for current API spelling, toolchain availability, macOS runtime support, and any code-shape fixes.
evals.expected_output: An advanced Swift Testing review that uses processExitsWith for exit tests, notes exit testing availability and supported runtime targets, fixes async Test.cancel sample shape, notes Swift 6.3/Xcode 26.4 availability for warning severity and image attachments, and records images with Attachment.record(..., as:).
assertions: States that exit testing requires Swift 6.2/Xcode 26.0 or newer and is supported for a macOS runtime target while not being available on iOS/tvOS/watchOS runtimes.
Mentions Swift 6.3 capture-list requirements when discussing captured parent-process values in exit tests.
Marks the Test.cancel example async when it awaits work and explains Test.cancel requires Swift 6.3/Xcode 26.4 or newer.
Uses Issue.record(..., severity: .warning) and image Attachment.record(..., named: ..., as: .png) with Swift 6.3/Xcode 26.4 availability.

evals.prompt: Plan tests for Scholium's macOS note workflow: unit-test frontmatter parsing, verify async autosave events, snapshot the reader in dark appearance, Increased Contrast, and enlarged reader typography, measure indexed-search performance, and automate opening, editing, and resolving a conflict. Which pieces should use Swift Testing, which should stay with XCTest/XCUITest or snapshot tooling, and how should the files be organized during migration?
evals.expected_output: A boundary-aware macOS test plan that uses Swift Testing for parser and async behavior tests, confirmation for autosave events, XCTest/XCUITest for UI automation and performance measurement, approved snapshot tooling for visual regression, and allows both frameworks in one target while keeping each test framework-pure.
assertions: Uses Swift Testing for pure unit logic such as frontmatter parsing.
Uses confirmation or structured concurrency for async autosave events instead of sleeps.
Keeps performance measurement and common snapshot testing flows in XCTest or dedicated snapshot tooling.
Covers macOS-specific visual states including light/dark appearance, Increased Contrast, and scalable reader typography where relevant.
States that XCTest and Swift Testing can coexist in a target during migration while keeping APIs from the two frameworks out of the same test.
